requirements.title: The data-ref supplies the actual argument for a passed-object dummy
requirements.definition: In a type-bound procedure reference or procedure pointer component reference that has a passed-object dummy argument, the data-ref of the function reference or call statement corresponds as the actual argument for that passed-object dummy.

pending.type-bound-data-ref-passed-object: Define a type with integer slot initialized to -9 and type-bound subroutine set(self,value); call obj%set(37) and expect obj%slot becomes 37 while another object sentinel remains -9.
pending.procedure-pointer-component-data-ref-pas: Use a procedure pointer component bound to the same passed-object subroutine, call obj%pp(43), and expect only obj%slot changes from -11 to 43.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish distinguished non-default state first, then observe portable single-image properties such as exact integer values, exact character values, PRESENT status, defined pointer-association inquiries, rank and bound inquiry results, and caller-side sentinels after procedure return. Unnumbered program restrictions do not create a required processor diagnostic; negative examples for those facets are source-control material only.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Diagnostics are not claimed unless a numbered constraint or syntax rule requires them. Undefined association status, undefined definition status, processor-dependent argument-passing mechanisms, storage addresses, descriptor layouts, and coarray/image behavior are not executable oracles here.
requirements.dependencies: Registered dependencies: clauses 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, and 13 for source form, type compatibility, declaration attributes, designators, array element order, expressions, execution constructs, data transfer, and formatting foundations already present in this suite. Unregistered dependencies retained for future fixtures: later clause 15 optional, pointer, allocatable, procedure, elemental, generic, pure/simple, sequence association, and finalization rules; clause 16 inquiry intrinsics and ISO_FORTRAN_ENV support; clauses 14, 17, 18, and 19 for modules, IEEE support, C interoperability, and association/lifetime state.
